get.description:
The one response body in this document that is not named by a schema: it
*is* the document, and describing it would mean carrying a copy of the
`OpenAPI` meta-schema.

The `Caller` is taken and dropped: it is not used, but taking it is what
makes this route authenticated — a handler that takes no `Caller` is open
by construction (see [`crate::auth::extract::Caller`]).

200.description: What was detected about this host

get.description:
The update status the web layer answers directly: the check fetches the
release feed over the network and lives in [`detent_update`], which the
operations engine does not depend on and cannot answer for. Read-only,
like every other endpoint in this module — **installing** an update is a
`write`-scoped, CSRF-checked `POST` that waits until the privileged swap
(PLAN §2.9 steps 5b–5c) actually lands; nothing here installs anything.

200.description: The update status under the configured policy

503.description: The release feed could not be reached

AffectedService.description: A service a change would affect.

actions.description: The actions the module declared, most preferred first.

unit.description: The unit name the monitor resolved for this host's init system.

ApiServiceCommand.description:
A [`ServiceCommand`](detent_ops::ServiceCommand), as a request body may
name it.

[`detent_ops::ServiceCommand`] cannot derive [`utoipa::ToSchema`] without
giving `detent-ops` a dependency on `utoipa`, which PLAN §2.1 forbids: the
operations layer stays front-end agnostic. This is the thin mirror that
lets a request body have a precise, documented schema anyway; it converts
straight to the real type and carries no behaviour of its own.

backed_up.description:
Whether a backup was retained, and therefore whether commit-confirm
has something to roll back to.

oneOf.description:
The armed commit-confirm window, for a module whose descriptor sets
`commit_confirm`.

created.description: Whether the target did not exist before.

oneOf.description: Digest of the replaced contents; `None` when the file was created.
The service action, when one was requested.

confirm_secs.description:
Commit-confirm window, in seconds. Omitted uses the module's default;
the monitor clamps whatever is armed either way.

expected_hash.description:
Digest the caller last read, as 64 lowercase hex characters. A
mismatch is refused (409) rather than silently overwriting somebody
else's edit.

oneOf.description: What to do to the module's service afterwards.
Replaced by the path of the temporary file holding the candidate config.

ArgTemplate.description: One argument of an [`ExternalCheck`] command line.

AuditRecord.description: One line of the audit log.

error_id.description: Fluent id of the failure, when it failed.

module.description: The module the operation was about, when it was about one.

prev_hash.description: Digest of the target before the operation, as 64 hex characters.

BackupId.description: Index into the backup listing most recently produced for a module.

created_unix_s.description: Modification time, seconds since the Unix epoch.

name.description:
File name of the backup within the module's backup directory. The
directory itself is never disclosed.

target.description: Which target the backup came from.

CertReport.description:
What the serving TLS certificate looks like: its fingerprint, when it
expires, and how much of its lifetime is left.

`not_after_unix` is `None` when the DER did not parse — reported as
"unknown", never a failure: status must work even when the parse does not.

fingerprint.description: Uppercase colon-separated SHA-256 of the DER, as printed at startup.

lifetime_used_percent.description:
Whole percent of `[not_before, not_after]` elapsed at read time, when
both endpoints parse. `None` means "unknown", not zero.

not_after_unix.description: Validity end, whole seconds since the Unix epoch, when parseable.

oneOf.description:
The program's output must contain this literal substring. Matching is a
plain substring search, not a regular expression: the core deliberately
carries no regex engine (PLAN §2.3), and the platform layer applies the
pattern as-is. Do not write anchors or metacharacters here — `^Loaded`
looks for a literal caret.

stdout_pattern.description:
The program's output must contain this literal substring. Matching is a
plain substring search, not a regular expression: the core deliberately
carries no regex engine (PLAN §2.3), and the platform layer applies the
pattern as-is. Do not write anchors or metacharacters here — `^Loaded`
looks for a literal caret.

CheckExpectation.description: How the result of an [`ExternalCheck`] is judged.

CheckReport.description: The result of running one of a module's upstream validators.

detail.description: A bounded excerpt of its output, or the reason it did not run.

exit_code.description: Exit status, when the program was executed.

passed.description: Whether the declared expectation was met.

program.description: Absolute path of the validator, for display.

ran.description:
Whether the validator actually ran. `false` means the binary is not
installed or the monitor has no check runner wired up — informative,
not a plan failure.

commit_id.description: The commit that is now final.

CommitId.description: Identifier the caller chooses for one commit-confirm cycle.

Diagnostic.description:
One validation finding.

Built with [`Diagnostic::new`] and refined with the `with_*` methods; every field
beyond severity and id is optional because not every finding maps to a field or a
byte range.

args.description: Named arguments for the Fluent message, sorted for deterministic output.

oneOf.description: The model field this finding is about, if any.

id.description: The Fluent id of the message.

oneOf.description: The byte range in the source file this finding is about, if any.

Diagnostics.description:
The findings from one call to `ConfigModule::validate`, in the order they were
produced.

DiffLine.description:
One line of a [`Hunk`], including its own line terminator when the source
line had one.

ErrorBody.description: The JSON body of every API failure.

code.description: A stable machine-readable class, derived from the status.

diagnostics.description:
Validation findings, only present for a rejected [`Operation::Apply`]
(PLAN §2.5: any `Severity::Error` diagnostic stops an apply before
anything is written). Mirrors `detent_core::diag::Diagnostics`, which
cannot derive `ToSchema` without giving `detent-core` a dependency on
`utoipa`.

[`Operation::Apply`]: detent_ops::Operation::Apply

message_id.description: The Fluent id a front end renders.

ExternalCheck.description:
An upstream validator run against a candidate file before it is installed, e.g.
`chronyd -p -f <tmp>` or `testparm -s <tmp>`.

program.description: Absolute path of the validator binary.

FieldPath.description:
A path to a field inside a module's model, in the style of a JSON pointer without
the leading slash: `"entries/3/hostnames/0"`.

The UI uses it to attach a diagnostic to the control that produced it.

HostProfile.description:
What is known about the host a module is producing configuration for.

Populated by `detent-platform`; the core only reads it. Modules use it to pick a
backend, to size defaults, and to hide options newer than the installed service.

hostname.description: The host's own name, used by defaults such as the `/etc/hosts` entry for it.

ram_mib.description: Physical memory in MiB, used to size caches and worker counts.

service_versions.description: Installed version per service name, e.g. `{"chronyd": "4.5"}`.

HostReport.description:
What was detected about this host.

A projection rather than [`Detected`] itself: `HostFacts` and its enums are
plain Rust types with no `Serialize`, and adding one there would mean
editing `detent-platform`.

distro_id.description: `ID=` from `/etc/os-release`, when the host has one.

Hunk.description:
One contiguous run of changes plus its surrounding context, addressed the
way a unified diff addresses it: 1-based line numbers, and a start of `0`
when the side contributes no lines at all.

new_lines.description: How many candidate lines this hunk covers.

new_start.description: First candidate line covered, 1-based; `0` when `new_lines` is `0`.

old_lines.description: How many original lines this hunk covers.

old_start.description: First original line covered, 1-based; `0` when `old_lines` is `0`.

InitSystem.description: The init system of the host being configured.

password.description: The password, in the clear over TLS 1.3 and nowhere else.

totp_code.description:
The six-digit TOTP code, when the account has a second factor enrolled
or `auth.totp_required` is set.

MessageId.description:
The id of a Fluent message in `locales/<lang>/core.ftl`.

Always a compile-time constant, so a module cannot accidentally emit a message
that has no translation entry.

model.description:
The candidate model, exactly as the shape `GET /modules/{id}`'s
`schema` field describes.

ModuleDescriptor.description: Everything a module declares about itself.

checks.description: Upstream validators run before installing a candidate file.

commit_confirm.description:
Whether a change to this module needs commit-confirm (it can lock an admin
out, e.g. network configuration).

display_name_id.description: Fluent id of the module's display name.

id.description:
Stable module id, e.g. `hosts`. Used in URLs, the CLI, the audit log and
feature names.

security_notes.description: Fluent ids of security notes shown alongside this module.

targets.description: Files and directories this module owns.

oneOf.description: Digest of the file the model came from.

model.description:
The model parsed from the file on disk, or `None` when the target
could not be read (e.g. it does not exist yet).

schema.description: The JSON Schema of its model, with `x-detent` UI hints.

OpKind.description:
The kind of an [`Operation`], with none of its payload.

This is what the audit log stores: an operation's arguments include the
candidate configuration, and PLAN §2.5 forbids the audit log from carrying
file bodies.

Os.description: The operating system family of the host being configured.

Owner.description: The account a [`Target`] must belong to after a write.

PathSpec.description: A filesystem path owned by a module. Always a compile-time constant.

PendingCommit.description: A commit-confirm window that is now running in the monitor.

deadline.description: When the window closes, RFC 3339 UTC.

rollback_targets.description: How many targets the monitor will roll back if it expires.

timeout_s.description: Seconds until automatic rollback, as the monitor clamped them.

affected_services.description: Services a subsequent apply could act on.

checks.description: Results of the module's upstream validators, run against the candidate.

current_hash.description: Digest of the file as it is now, to pass back as `expected_hash`.

diagnostics.description: Validation findings for the candidate model.

path.description: The target this plan is about.

rendered.description: The candidate file, rendered in full.

unified_diff.description:
`diff` as unified-diff text, so a front end and the CLI show the same
bytes without each re-implementing the rendering.

would_change.description: Whether applying would change anything at all.

new_hash.description: Digest now on disk, 64 lowercase hex characters.

target.description: The target that was put back, as the monitor's index for it.

commit_id.description: The commit that was rolled back.

restored.description: How many targets were actually restored.

ServiceAction.description: What may be done to a service after a config change.

ServiceBinding.description: A service a module's files configure.

actions.description: Actions this module may request, most preferred first.

units.description: Names of the service per init system.

ServiceCommand.description:
What a caller may ask be done to a service.

A closed mirror of [`CoreServiceAction`] that, unlike the core type, is
`Deserialize` (so it can arrive over an API) and, unlike the wire type,
has no `Status` variant — status is [`Operation::ServiceStatus`], which
mutates nothing and must not be confusable with an action that does.

active.description: Whether the unit is running afterwards.

unit.description: The unit the monitor acted on.

enabled.description:
Whether the unit starts automatically at boot, when the backend can
determine it.

oneOf.description:
When the unit entered its current state, when the backend can
determine it.

unit.description:
The unit name actually resolved and queried, i.e. the alternative
from [`UnitNames`] that exists on this host.

SessionView.description:
What `GET /api/v1/auth/session` answers.

The session **id** is deliberately absent: the browser already holds it in
a `HttpOnly` cookie, and a copy of it in a readable response body would
undo that.

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds until the session expires, idle and absolute limits combined.

subject.description: The user this session belongs to.

totp_satisfied.description: Whether a second factor was presented.

Sha256Digest.description: A SHA-256 digest, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

Span.description:
A byte range within the text a [`Document`] was parsed from.

`start` is inclusive, `end` is exclusive. Both are byte offsets, not character
offsets, and always fall on UTF-8 boundaries.

State.description: The run state of a service, as reported by [`ServiceManager::status`].

SystemTimeView.description:
How `serde` renders a [`SystemTime`]: two integers, not an RFC 3339
string.

It exists only so the `openapi` feature has something accurate to point
[`ServiceStatus::since`] at — `utoipa` has no schema for [`SystemTime`],
and describing it as a string would misdescribe the bytes clients receive.
Nothing constructs one.

secs_since_epoch.description: Whole seconds since the Unix epoch.

Target.description: One file or directory a module manages.

mode.description: The mode the target must end up with, e.g. `0o644`.

owner.description: The owner the target must end up with.

TargetId.description: Index into the monitor's target table.

TargetKind.description: What kind of filesystem object a [`Target`] is.

UnitNames.description:
Per-init-system names for one service, most preferred first.

Distributions disagree (`chronyd.service` on Fedora, `chrony.service` on Debian),
so each backend gets a list of alternatives rather than a single name.

bsdrc.description: BSD `rc.d` script names. Kept for portability; BSD is a deferred tier.

UpdateReport.description:
The answer body of `GET /api/v1/system/update`.

A mirror of [`CheckReport`], not a re-export: `detent-update` has no
`utoipa` dependency by design (PLAN §2.1 keeps the update crate
front-end agnostic), so this is the thin mirror that documents the schema,
the same move [`super::ApiServiceCommand`] makes for `ServiceCommand`.
Field-for-field identical and converted, never copied by hand.

published.description: When the release was published, RFC 3339.

security.description: Whether it bypassed the age gate via `detent-security: true`.

tag.description: The qualifying tag, when one exists.

Upstream.description: The upstream project whose configuration format a module tracks.

docs.description: Documentation URLs shown in the UI.

release_feed.description: A release feed URL the upstream-watch workflow polls, when one exists.

tracked_version.description: The upstream release this module's option set was derived from.
